title: Tutorial 1: Keychain tag
subtitle: Steps, boxes, cylinders, cutting a hole, and exporting for 3D printing

steps.chapter: A design is a list of steps

steps.caption: A SketchBillet design is a list of steps, like a recipe. The tag takes three: a plate, a cylinder for the hole, and the cut.
Click Box on the Model tab. It adds a 20 mm box.
Properties shows the new step. Call it Plate.
Make it 60 mm wide (x), 30 mm deep (y) and 4 mm tall (z).
Click Fit all, under the view, to see the whole part. The mouse wheel zooms in and out.
The box starts at the origin, 0, 0, 0. x goes right, y goes back and z goes up.
Cylinder is in the Create dropdown. This one becomes the hole.
A hole 5 mm across: a radius of 2.5 mm.
Make it 6 mm tall, and start it 1 mm below the plate, so it pokes out of both faces.
Put it 9 mm from the left edge, in the middle of the 30 mm depth: x 9, y 15, z -1.
Pick Plate in the feature tree, then hold Ctrl and pick Hole. The first one picked is kept; the second is cut away.
Click Cut.
Call the new step Tag.
Turn the view to look at it: drag on an empty part of the view.

steps.chapter: Step 4: Check it and export it

steps.caption: File > Check for Printing checks it's closed all round, with no wall too thin.
File > Export writes a file for your 3D printer's slicer.
Call it tag.stl, and save it.

steps.chapter: Step 5: Choose what it's made of

steps.caption: Every body is PLA until you pick a material. Printing in PETG? Pick Plate, and choose PETG. The tag is cut from the plate, so it's PETG too.
Properties shows the tag's mass in PETG.
File > Save as keeps the design, so you can change any step later.
Done! Next: Tutorial 2, the desk organizer.
